description: The dimensions a decomposition can cover, and the three states of coverage.

content._doc:
The dimensions a thing can have. A slot spec says how much of a frame is FILLED; this says whether the frame was ever DRAWN. entity.person declared zero temporal slots, and nothing in the system could tell that apart from a person who happens to have no dates — the spec cannot report a question it never asked.

DERIVED, NOT INVENTED. Every dimension below is a grouping of slot families that already exist across the 19 governed specs (measured 2026-08-09): summary 35, evidence 30, identifiers 27, identity 24, spatial 21, source 17, temporal 9, relationships 4. The dimensions name what the corpus already distinguishes; they do not impose a taxonomy on it.

THREE STATES, the same trichotomy as filled/blocked/empty:
  covered         the spec declares at least one slot in this dimension
  not_applicable  the spec says so explicitly — considered and ruled out
  NEVER ASKED     neither — the honest gap, and the only one that is a finding

identity.label: Identity
identity.doc: What names this thing and settles which one it is.

physical.label: Physical
physical.doc: What it is made of or measures — a body, a hull, a tonnage.

temporal.label: Temporal
temporal.doc: When it happened, or over what period it held. A thing with no temporal dimension cannot have a history.

relational.label: Relational
relational.doc: What it is connected to — participants, ownership, registration, membership.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.doc: Where the claim came from and how well attested it is.

descriptive.label: Descriptive
descriptive.doc: Prose about the thing. Present in almost every spec, and the weakest dimension — a headline is not knowledge.

content._spec_level_note: A spec may declare `dimension: <name>`, meaning every slot it contains belongs to that dimension. Used by sub-concept specs whose slots are bare leaf names scoped by the node type rather than by a family prefix.
